Unforgettable
Oct 2018 • Friends
We ordered razor clams, king prawns, clams, morning glories, fried rice with beef and fried noodles with beef. Wait for 10 minutes, the fried rice and noodles arrived but the toppings becomes seafood but not beef. Obviously wrong order, however we were too hungry so we just eat. Then we found out the seafood was not fresh and very tough. The fried rice was unbelievably hard and chewy. We cannot finish them. Then wait for another 30 minutes, our main course still hadn’t arrived, we chased the server, he said they are coming. Another 20 minutes passed, we chased again and finally arrived. The razor clams were full of sand and the prawns were just came out from hot water. We could not eat at all. The service was terrible even our expectations are low before going in. The dining room was dirty and the toilet was awful. Avoid to try unless you are not hungry or you are looking for trouble.

By far the worst experience of Vietnamese restaurants (and beyond)
Jul 2017 • Family
Be aware of this restaurant! We had lunch tonight there, at least we wanted to have one. We were given the menue and noted that no prices were indicated. We were told that we would be informed of the prices when asking for specific plates. Due to next to nonexisting knowledge of English of the waiters, this was not the case. 
They try to attract customers by showing them containers of living fish, from lobster to crabs. But if you look carefully, you will also see squid and other fish lying around at 35 degrees without being cooled, quite dangerous. Will you be served the fresh or the rotten fish? Unfortunately, the unfriendly waitress was unable to understand my questions concerning the freshness of fish prepared. The menu showed no drinks, only about 12 different dishes of which 5 or 6 were not available. We ordered one rice plate with egg, two rice plates with sea food and 2 rice plates with shrimps. My wife ordered a coke, the waiter brought 5. We told him that we only ordered one coke. He left then and nobody was interested what the other 4 members of our family would like to drink. There were 3 waiters and besides us only 4 guests. Nobody cared about us. We had to go to them interrupting their playing around with smartphone and asking for drinks. No drinks were cold. I ordered a beer and was served a Heineken. I asked in my rudimentary Vietnamese whether there was not Vietnamese beer like Saigon beer. I was told No. So I accompanied the waiter to the bar and found several local beers like Tiger beer. 
Finally, three of the 5 plates we ordered, arrived. We would have needed a microscope to discover elements different from rice in the plates, only two tiny pieces of shrimp in the sea food plate, no other signs of fish and no signs of eggs in the rice plate with egg. The plates with shrimps never arrived. So principally, we were only served rice!!! Disgusting rice!!! But we may have been lucky not to have received the seafood ordered which due to bad cooling conditions might have caused harm to us.

So we asked for the bill and were shocked again as they tried to charge us 150000 VNDs for each disgusting rice plate which could hardly be sold in Vietnam for more than 15000 VNDs. In addition, they had charged us 3 plates of rice with seafood food instead of 2 and an another with nonexistent egg.

As no prices were indicated and as they were unable to cite prices before ordering, they were somehow entitled to do it, but it was clearly fraud and a kind of unarmed robbery. After my protest, they modified the bill somehow still way too expensive.

So if you want to be charged a lot of money for miserable food not corresponding to its description, for nonexisting and unfriendly service where you have to search for the waiters and for being cheated, then go for it. But you could instead go somewhere else. The Vietnamese kitchen is one of the best worldwide. With the amount you would spend in this miserable restaurant for nothing, you could offer yourself a fantastic evening in thousands of true Vietnamese restaurants.

Very Expensive - eat in town less than half the cost
Feb 2015 • Friends
We are a group of 28 Malaysians and arranged our own tour. Driver and local tour guide took the group here which looks very local without the upmarket settings. Some members took the trouble to ask the price of fried rice and was quoted Rm20 (USD6) per person. They were appalled at this high cost and stood up to walk off. The owners then 'discounted' it to Rm20 for two persons. Anyway all 28 members only ordered cheap fried rice and noodles. Big lobster cost on the notice board states Dong 2,600,000 (USD125) PER KILO NOT PER PIECE. Rest of the seafood i.e. fish and shellfish are also VERY EXPENSIVE. Noted that to Europeans and Japanese, prices here are reasonable compared to at home prices. But for most of us Asians, including Malaysian, Thais and Chinese, prices are VERY HIGH. Some of our members flew in a few days earlier to catch the cheaper flights and ate at another local seafood place at a third of the price. So stay away from eateries facing the famed CHINA BEACH and have your meals in town. If your Tour Leader recommends this place, go check the prices b4 taking a seat, then very assertively ask your Tour Leader to take you to downtown for your meals. You can probably find many good eateries around the Hotel you stay. My gut feelings is that the Driver and Tour Leader gets a cut of the Expensive Cost of the meals here.
